name: Dolomite
rootCause: On March 20th, Dolomite, a decentralized trading protocol in the Arbitrum ecosystem, was attacked due to a vulnerability in its old contracts on the Ethereum mainnet. Approximately 187 victims suffered asset losses totaling $1.8 million, including 1,245,271 USDC, 94,423 DAI, and 165.9 WETH. As of March 24th, Dolomite has recovered 90% of the assets taken by the attacker.

descriptions.text: On March 20th, Dolomite, a decentralized trading protocol in the Arbitrum ecosystem, was attacked due to a vulnerability in its old contracts on the Ethereum mainnet. Approximately 187 victims suffered asset losses totaling $1.8 million, including 1,245,271 USDC, 94,423 DAI, and 165.9 WETH. As of March 24th, Dolomite has recovered 90% of the assets taken by the attacker.

Dolomite's legacy Loopring-based contract on Ethereum Mainnet was exploited on March 20, 2024, exposing users with lingering token approvals. Approximately $1.8 million in USDC, DAI, and WETH was stolen from 187 victims. The team recovered most assets and reimbursed remaining losses. The incident resulted from excessive gas-saving optimizations and defensive coding in a legacy Loopring Trade Delegate contract. Attackers were able to manipulate order state, bypass signature validation, and trigger unauthorized withdrawals from wallets holding stale ERC-20 approvals.
